---
name: phone-mockup
description: >-
  Use when the user sends one or more phone app screenshots and wants them
  placed in an iPhone frame on a white, dark, gradient, light-tinted, or
  custom-color background for posting, optionally with their logo at the bottom.
---
# iPhone screenshot mockups

Turn app screenshots into polished PNGs: the screenshot inside a realistic iPhone on a styled background. Core rule: **every phone is exactly the same pixel size**, within one image and across images. Never scale a phone to its screenshot. Screenshots are fitted into a fixed screen area instead.

## One-time setup
If `/home/box/tools/phone-mockup/mockup.py` does not exist, have an executor build it (Python 3, Pillow, numpy, no network at runtime) to the spec below, then test it with synthetic screenshots and view the outputs. Keep all defaults in one `config.json`.

CLI: `python3 mockup.py shot1.png [shot2.png ...] [options] --out out.png`

### Fixed size
Phone size depends only on `--width` (default 1440 gives a 1440x1920 canvas for one phone, body about 713x1500 px) or `--phone-height`. It must not depend on the screenshot, phone count, padding, gap, aspect, logo, or floor effect. Include a test that renders single, multi-phone, `--separate`, odd-aspect, different-padding, logo on/off, and floor on/off cases and asserts every phone body measures identical pixels.

### Frame geometry (fractions of phone body width pw, height ph)
- Body aspect (w/h) 0.4756, corner radius 0.205*pw, superellipse-like corners (exponent about 3).
- Silver titanium rim 0.015*pw, then black bezel 0.024*pw, so the screen is inset about 0.039*pw. Screen corner radius about 85 px at 537 px width.
- Dynamic Island: 31% of screen width wide, 8.8% of screen width tall, 3.1% below screen top, with a faint camera dot.
- Side buttons protruding 0.006*pw: left at 0.212-0.252, 0.29-0.358, 0.384-0.442 of ph; right at 0.31-0.425.
- Soft shadow mostly below: black alpha 0.28, blur sigma 0.013*ph, offset 0.01*ph down.
- Render at 3x supersample and downsample; clip the screenshot to the rounded screen.
- Frame colors: silver (default), black, white, titanium, blue, orange, or a hex.

### Layout
- Default padding 0.14*phone height above and below, phone centered; canvas at least 3:4 (width/height 0.75). `--padding` below 1 is a fraction of phone height, 1 or more is pixels.
- Multiple screenshots go side by side with gap 0.22*phone width by default (`--gap`, negative overlaps). `--separate` writes one image per screenshot. `--aspect W:H` grows the canvas without resizing phones.
- Fit: `--fit auto|cover|contain`. Auto crops to fill if the screenshot aspect is within 12% of an iPhone's, else letterboxes; warn above 10% off. Anchor top so the status bar stays.

### Backgrounds
- `white` (#FFFFFF, default), `cloud` (#F8F9FB), `dark` (navy radial glow #243050 to #06070B), plus radial presets graphite (#2E323D to #07070A), purple (#4B2A8C to #07040F), gold (#7A5A14 to #0A0803), emerald (#0E5A47 to #030A08), and colorful radials sunset (#FFA066, #FF4F7E, #4A1F8F), ocean (#6FE0FF, #2B7BFF, #10277F), aurora (#9AF5D0, #22B8A8, #1B2C85). `lavender` is a linear light gradient (#F3E8FF, #C9B6FF, #8E7BFF at 145 degrees).
- **Radial glow** (the look people like): a soft colored glow centered on the phone fading to near-black at the edges. Defaults: center (0.5, 0.5) of the canvas, radius 0.31 of the canvas diagonal, vertical stretch (aspect) 1.7 so it is narrow at the sides and tall above and below, smoothstep falloff, triangular +/-1 dithering to avoid banding. Options: `--gradient-type radial|linear`, `--glow-center x,y`, `--glow-radius`, `--glow-aspect`, `--glow-strength`, `--gradient-angle` (CSS degrees, linear only).
- `auto`: k-means on the saturated pixels of the screenshots. For dark screenshots build a radial glow of the dominant color on a near-black edge; for light ones a soft analogous linear gradient. Avoid muddy grey/brown results.
- Custom: `--bg-color` alone is solid; with `--bg-color2`, color 1 is the center glow and color 2 the edge.

### Light tinted looks with a floor (light-gold and friends)
A very light, subtle tinted radial with the phone appearing to sit on a surface. Best with a dark screenshot in a black frame (`--phone-color black`).
- Presets: `light-gold` (alias `warm`; radial glow #FCF2E6 near the phone fading to soft warm grey #CFC9C6 at the edges, radius 0.324, vertical stretch 1.7, plus a near-white wash #FEF9F6 over the top half), and the same recipe in other hues: `light-blue`, `light-rose`, `light-mint`. Keep the tint subtle: the background must stay light, never yellow or heavy (a stronger gold was tried and rejected as too much).
- `--bg auto-light` (alias `light`): same look, with the tint hue taken from the screenshot's dominant saturated color (gold from a gold-accented screenshot, violet from a purple one); greyscale screenshots get a neutral warm white.
- **Floor effect** (`--floor on|off`, `--floor-strength N`, `--reflection-strength N`; on automatically for the light presets and auto-light, off for everything else): painted only outside the phone body, so size and position never change. It adds a bright horizon band just above the phone's bottom edge, a slightly cooler floor below it, a faint warm pool of light under the phone, a tight dark contact shadow (alpha about 0.3, thickness about 0.4% of ph) with a wider faint spread shadow, and a very faint blurred mirrored reflection of the phone's lower edge (opacity about 0.16, fading out within about 7% of phone height). Everything is subtle; the goal is the feeling of sitting on something.
- Put all of these numbers in `config.json` so they are tunable.

### Optional logo (watermark)
Users can upload their own logo and choose to include it or not.
- Input: any logo as a JPG with a white or black background, or a PNG with alpha. Auto-prepare it: trim the empty margin; if there is no alpha, derive a transparent mask from luminance (detect whether it is dark-on-light or light-on-dark from the corner color) with clean anti-aliased edges and no halo. Cache the prepared transparent PNG in a `logo/` folder next to the tool.
- Placement: centered horizontally at the bottom, in the padding below the phone, about 12% of the single-phone canvas width, with its bottom about 5% of canvas height above the bottom edge. Never overlap the phone, its shadow, or the floor reflection; if the padding is too small, grow the canvas height (the phone stays the same size) and print a note. Multi-phone image: one logo centered under the group. `--separate`: a logo on every image.
- Color: `--logo-color auto|black|white|original`. Auto picks white or black from the actual rendered pixels behind the logo (works on gradients), so it always contrasts; a clearly multi-colored logo keeps its own colors.
- Flags: `--logo [PATH]` includes a logo for this run (and with a PATH, uses that file), `--no-logo` forces it off, `--logo-size`, `--logo-bottom`, `--logo-opacity`, and `--logo-default on|off` to make it always on or off via `config.json`. Ship with it off until the user supplies a logo.

## Using it
1. Save attachments to the box and run the tool. Default to white unless the user says otherwise; for dark or gradient asks use `dark`, a preset, or `auto` (pick a hue that matches the screenshot); for a light, subtle, or sitting-on-a-surface ask use `light-gold` or `auto-light` with a black frame.
2. Include the logo only when the user wants it or has set it as default.
3. Look at every output before sending. Check the island, rounded corners, that the phone size matches earlier images, and that the logo is crisp and contrasting.
4. Send the PNGs as attachments with one short line. Offer one specific tweak (stronger glow, different color, more space).
5. When the user asks for a change ("smaller glow", "more space"), adjust flags and rerender. When they approve a look, make it the new default in `config.json` and save it to memory.

---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner of the iPhone Screenshot Bot: learn their
  style and logo, and get them sending screenshots.
---
# Getting started

You turn app screenshots into clean iPhone mockups on white, dark, gradient, light-tinted, or custom-color backgrounds, with an optional logo at the bottom. Open with one friendly line saying that, then ask one thing at a time:

1. Ask them to send a first screenshot, or several. Work on it right away with the default look (silver iPhone, white background, generous even padding, no logo), so they see a result in the first minute.
2. After they see it, ask which background they usually want: white, dark glow, a colorful gradient, a soft light tint with a floor shadow, or colors pulled from the screenshot.
3. Ask if they want their own logo or handle at the bottom of the image. If yes, ask them to upload it (a JPG or PNG on a plain white or black background works) and show one render with it. Ask whether it should be on by default or only when they ask.
4. Ask if they have an X account or a few posts whose style they like. If so, look at the images with the X tools, measure phone size, padding, and background, and adopt it as their default.
5. Ask about spacing: tight, default, or roomy white space around the phone.
6. Ask whether they usually post one screenshot per image or several side by side.

Then: set the `phone-mockup` tool up if it is missing (see that skill), write their choices into memory (background, spacing, frame color, layout, logo on or off), update the tool's defaults, and tell them they can just send screenshots anytime. Remember: the phone is always the same size in every image.
